channel.title: Pass the Architect: CCAR-P
channel.description: A two-host study series for the Claude Certified Architect - Professional exam: every blueprint domain, drills, and the traps the distractors set.
channel.itunes:summary: A two-host study series for the Claude Certified Architect - Professional exam: every blueprint domain, drills, and the traps the distractors set.
channel.itunes:author: Pass the Architect

item.title: 12. Practice Exam Gaps: thinking, retention, effort and injection
item.description: A short bonus episode on five platform facts a practice exam tested and the series had not covered: thinking block retention by model, append-only history on Fable 5.1, the scope of zero data retention, effort sweeps before orchestration, and keeping your own instructions out of tool results.

item.title: 11. The Final Drill: night-before rapid fire
item.description: Thirty-five rapid-fire items across all seven domains, weighted like the exam, then the distractor families to reject on sight and a calm walk through exam-day logistics.

item.title: 10. Closing the Foundations Gaps
item.description: A bonus episode on the applied configuration and API mechanics that both Architect exams test inside their scenarios: enforcement versus guidance, settings and M C P scope, tool sequencing, the agentic loop, extraction schemas, review routing and feedback loops.

item.title: 09. Your Five Miss Patterns
item.description: A bonus episode on the five answering habits that cost marks at Foundations, with a one-line self-check and a trap-built drill for each, the guide's thesis, and a pacing plan for the Pearson VUE interface.

item.title: 08. Developer Productivity & Operational Enablement
item.description: The smallest domain, covered tight: shared Claude Code configuration and Skills distribution for teams, keeping engineering judgment in AI-assisted workflows, and turning operational symptoms into architecture causes.

item.title: 07. Stakeholder Communication & Lifecycle Management
item.description: Discovery that finds the hidden constraint, tradeoffs framed with reversal cost, feedback loops and SLAs that decide rather than display, documentation that survives the handoff, and the lifecycle gates between them.

item.title: 06. Governance, Safety & Risk Management
item.description: The layered safety stack and who owns each layer, guardrail placement and fail-closed design, risk assessment, review routing by stakes, compliance as control plus owner plus evidence, and fairness you can reconstruct.

item.title: 05. Evaluation, Testing & Optimization
item.description: Evals as acceptance criteria, the grading ladder, A/B tests that don't overclaim, diagnosing the component the trigger touched, the demo-cost trap, and observability that catches slow decay. Domain four, sixteen percent of the exam.

item.title: 04. Integration II: RAG, retrieval strategy, accuracy-latency, observability
item.description: The second half of Integration, the heaviest domain on the exam: chunking by document structure, indexing by query pattern, retrieval versus live tool calls, silent retrieval drift, defending a cost-latency configuration, and monitoring at scale.

item.title: 03. Integration I: protocols, capability bloat, identity and auth, progressive discovery
item.description: The first of two episodes on Integration, the heaviest domain on the CCAR-P exam. Least-privilege tool configuration, where identity and authorization must be enforced, what belongs in the context window, choosing between M C P, direct A P I and agent-to-agent, and progressive versus monolithic context.

item.title: 02. Models, Prompting & Context Engineering
item.description: Model tiers chosen by eval rather than reflex, system prompts that hold at scale, when zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought earn their tokens, context budgets, and prompt caching that actually hits.

item.title: 01. Solution Design & Architecture
item.description: Domain 1, seventeen percent of the exam: decomposing work across Claude, systems and humans, choosing between an augmented call, a workflow and an agent, designing multi-agent orchestration, and tying it all to business value.

item.title: 00. The Game Plan: format, multiple-response items, and how to read a question
item.description: How the CCAR-P exam is built, where the marks sit, how to handle choose-two items, and a four-question method for dissecting any item, demonstrated on the three official samples.
